answers.answer: An Exile who takes the Oathkeeper title during Act cannot win as Usurper at the next Wake: at that Wake, the victory check happens first, then the title flips to Usurper. The first ordinary Usurper win check is the following Wake. If round eight ends first while they still hold the title Usurper-side, the endgame priority can award them victory then. If they lose the title before winning, they cannot win as Usurper; retaking it gives them the Oathkeeper side and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘From taking Oathkeeper during Act, the normal sequence is next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake or at the end of round 8… Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it…’

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. The extra requirement for any Visionary win is that the Exile must have drawn at least 3 Visions from the world deck. For a ‘most’ Vision goal (Conquest or Sanctuary), the claimant must have strictly more than every other player; a tie does not count.
answers.evidence: Oath table lists the four Oath/Vision pairs; Visionary victory says ‘at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck’ and for Conquest/Sanctuary ‘most’ means ‘strictly more than every other player, no ties.’

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. The Chancellor wins, unless a Citizen meets the Successor goal, in which case that Citizen wins alone. An Exile Oathkeeper or Usurper prevents the roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime: ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7; roll only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper; results ‘6 / 5–6 / 3–6’; ‘An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.’

answers.answer: Round eight ends automatically. Priority is: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins (Chancellor unless a qualified Successor); (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions resolved Conquest, then Rebellion, then Sanctuary, then Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless a qualified Successor), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion lists the exact four-step endgame priority and the Vision priority order.

answers.answer: Successor goals: Supremacy—hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen; People—hold Darkest Secret; Protection—hold People's Favor; Devotion—hold Grand Scepter. A Citizen cannot win by a revealed Vision or by becoming Usurper. The Successor goal does not end the game on its own; it replaces a Chancellor win when one would occur.
answers.evidence: Oath table gives each Citizen Successor goal. Visionary victory states Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper; War exhaustion says Successor resolves whenever Chancellor would win and never ends the game on its own.

answers.answer: At Wake, if you hold People's Favor, choose to put 1 favor from your board onto it or return 1 favor from it to the least-full suit bank (choosing among tied banks). You may not remove its last favor: when it has 1, add 1 if able; if you have none, do nothing. If it is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After these choices, flip it to Mob if it has at least 6 favor. If it reaches the threshold at this final check, there is no extra repeat for that Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake step 1 specifies add-or-return, least-full bank and tie choice, preserving last favor, repeating once if already Mob-side, and checking 6+ afterward without retroactive repetition.

answers.answer: Rest in order: return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; return secrets on denizens, edifices and relics to your board and flip facedown secrets on your board faceup; refresh Supply; move the marker one extra space left for each unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost space (7 Supply); then resolve optional Rest powers, each once in an order you choose. Exiles and the Chancellor refresh according to warbands remaining in their personal bank: Chancellor 18+ = 6, 11–17 = 5, 4–10 = 4, 0–3 = 3; Exile 9+ = 6, 4–8 = 5, 0–3 = 4. A Citizen refreshes to the exact space of the Chancellor's marker, including leftmost; do not count purple warbands to determine it. The saved Supply movement is an additional leftward adjustment after refresh.
answers.evidence: Rest mandatory order, steps 1–5, including refresh thresholds, exact Citizen marker-space rule, and saved Supply adjustment.

answers.answer: Search uses either the world deck or the discard pile for the region where your pawn is, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret changes the world-deck cost to 2, with other modifiers still applying. Draw 3 unless the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw; you cannot choose to stop early. From the world deck, draw one at a time and stop immediately on a Vision, announcing it and advancing Visions Drawn by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop drawing or advance that track.
answers.evidence: Search section gives the source/cost rules and states that a world-deck Vision stops drawing and advances Visions Drawn, while a discard-pile Vision does neither.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle; choose the order when discarding multiple cards. A card from hand or advisers goes to the pile for your pawn's region. If discarding a card at a site in another region, use that card's region. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank. Secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: Discard destinations paragraph states the region cycle, the different handling of hand/adviser cards versus remote-site cards, and where favor and secrets go.

answers.answer: Advisers are limited to 3 total, counting both faceup and facedown. Before exceeding the limit, discard an adviser, subject to card locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, apply the new limit before playing it, using the lowest limit if multiple cards change it. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner or power, and any card (including site-only cards and Visions) can be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action. Faceup advisers cannot be freely discarded; they can be discarded only when another rule permits or requires it. A true Vision played faceup by an Exile goes in the separate Revealed Vision space, not an adviser slot, replacing and discarding the prior revealed Vision. Chancellor and Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser/true Vision options state the limit, facedown rules and later minor-action options; true Visions use the Revealed Vision slot and replace the old one.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: put 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site, then take 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board (Citizens take purple). You need not rule the site. Relics and ruins are ineligible, and ruling a remote site does not allow a remote Muster. Trade costs 1 Supply and also requires an empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site. Choose one: put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 favor per matching faceup adviser from that card's suit bank; or put 2 favor on it to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. Facedown advisers do not match. With no matching faceup advisers, the second Trade gains zero secrets, but the 2 favor cost is still paid. Gains are limited by finite favor/warband supply; secrets are unlimited. Relics and ruins cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections specify their costs, eligible cards, payment and gains, with no matching advisers yielding zero secrets for the 2-favor option.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. You may Recover a facedown relic at your site, paying its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in your personal bank. Or Recover either banner from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by paying strictly more of the corresponding resource than it currently has. For People's Favor, place the paid favor on the banner; distribute its old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at a bank you choose and proceeding through printed bank order; do not return it to the previous holder, and flip it to normal side if Mob. For Darkest Secret, place the paid secrets on it; the new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. If recovering it from yourself, all old secrets return to you; if from shared bank, the remainder stays there. Recovering a banner has no seizure penalty.
answers.evidence: Recover section gives the relic cost, strict banner outbid, handling of old resources, Mob flip and no-seizure-penalty rule.

answers.answer: To Recover Darkest Secret from another player, there must be a suited card at that player's pawn site that matches none of their faceup advisers. An empty site or a site with only a ruin protects the banner; a ruin and facedown advisers have no suit. If the holder has no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable. Recovering from yourself or the shared bank ignores this protection. The summary does not describe a distinct ‘no cards’ case beyond the empty-site rule; an empty site is protected.
answers.evidence: Darkest Secret protection: ‘there must be a suited card at their pawn's site matching none of their faceup advisers’; ‘Empty sites and ruin-only sites protect it’; if no faceup advisers but a suited site card exists, it is recoverable.

answers.answer: For a Campaign, choose as defender any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. Declare at least one target at your pawn's site; if the defender rules that site, you must target it. You may also target any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map, with 1 defense die each. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may instead/additionally target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and favor together (2 dice). A relic belonging to a co-located defender can itself satisfy the local-target requirement, including one at the same site.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2 give defender eligibility and targets, including remote sites and co-located relic/banner/pawn-and-favor targets; the summary explicitly says a co-located relic target satisfies the local requirement.

answers.answer: The attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force. Apply applicable modifiers and mandatory Oathkeeper (+1 defense die) or Usurper (+2 defense dice) bonus. Defender rolls defense first: count shields, doubling shields for each double-symbol (multipliers stack), then add all defending warbands at targeted sites, the defender's board force if their pawn is at the attacker site or any targeted site, and 1 for each targeted bandit site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Attacker rolls afterward: each skull kills 1 of the attacker's own force warbands; count full swords, plus 1 for each pair of hollow swords (an unpaired hollow sword counts zero). The attacker may sacrifice surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower loses. The defeated side kills half its remaining force, rounded down, and returns survivors to its board; bandits cannot be killed. In Imperial defense, the Chancellor chooses which defending Imperial warbands die, with site survivors returning to Chancellor's board and surviving Citizen board warbands staying on their boards.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2 and 4–6 specify dice, defense components, skulls, hollow swords, exact sacrifices, strict-win/tie rule and defeat casualties; Imperial defense adds Chancellor's casualty choice.

answers.answer: After an attacker wins, they may place any number of surviving force warbands, including zero, on any targeted sites. Placing zero can leave a site to bandits unless another power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. A banner seized by Campaign (or another way except Recover) has 2 resources burned, to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site at no Supply, and may independently burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; if Shrouded Wood's enemy ruler chooses the destination, that overrides the attacker's choice. Resolve battle-plan effects in order: defeated effects after defeat casualties, attacker site/relic/banner/banishment results, victorious effects, and finally ‘At end, discard’ instructions. Transfer Supremacy title at the end of Campaign, not during temporary loss of site rule.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 7–8 state all post-victory outcomes, zero garrisons, banner seizure penalty, optional banishment and favor burn, Shrouded Wood override and timing of effects/title transfer.

answers.answer: When an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as an Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker site or any targeted site. All relevant modifiers ruled by the defender and Allies apply, and the title defense bonus is shared on the defending side even outside Supremacy. Allied board warbands contribute defense only if their pawn is at the attacker site or a targeted site. The defending side may use plans at Imperial sites and its own advisers, but not other players' advisers; each plan can be used only once per Campaign, and its user pays. The declared defender chooses order, timing and priority if Allies disagree. The Chancellor chooses which Imperial defending warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving Citizen board warbands stay on those boards. In a Citizen's Campaign against Chancellor or another Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; if the Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it. This does not make all Citizens non-Imperial in an intra-Empire Campaign.
answers.evidence: Imperial defense bullets specify automatic Chancellor ally, Citizen allies, shared modifiers/title bonus, eligible plans and warbands, declared defender's authority, casualty handling and temporary non-Imperial status.

answers.answer: Base Travel costs by origin/destination region are: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, Cradle 2, Provinces 2, Hinterland 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not necessarily adjacent. If the destination is facedown, reveal it, place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and its printed number of facedown relics from the relic deck beside it. Pay the fixed-number cost first, then apply other increases/decreases. A power that says to spend no Supply is the final override and makes Supply payment zero even if another effect increases it. Site entry restrictions still apply unless expressly ignored.
answers.evidence: Travel table and text give all region costs, destination reveal/stocking, order of fixed cost and modifiers, and free Travel as final override.

answers.answer: During play, the Grand Scepter holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, but cannot offer on the turn they took the Scepter. The offer must promise exactly one Reliquary relic; it may also include a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners or non-Reliquary relics, and the recipient may be allowed to peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics. On acceptance, the Exile flips to Citizen and replaces their own board and map warbands with purple (if the purple supply is short, they choose which to remove/replace); they discard a revealed Vision, flip their Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end their Act if it is their turn, refresh to full leftmost Supply, exchange the promised pieces, and the Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. A forced-Citizenship power applies acceptance without a negotiated offer. The Scepter holder may also exile a Citizen under the stated separate procedure, but that is not an offer/acceptance exchange.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile section gives Scepter offer timing, required and optional exchange contents, acceptance changes, forced Citizenship and separate exile procedure.

answers.answer: If the winner won by a Vision alone, the next Oath must match that Vision. If victory was by any other way or by multiple methods, choose any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards (including boxed boards) to Exile; the winner may offer Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped. Chronicle offers ignore normal in-play requirements: no Reliquary relic, resource payment or Scepter permission. An accepting Exile flips to Citizen and replaces each garrison at every site they rule with exactly one warband of the winner's color, regardless of previous garrison size. Rebuild the world deck by shuffling denizens remaining in play (excluding cards at sites, in Archive or Dispossessed), then put 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions in the 12-card top stack; 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions in the 18-card middle stack; and remaining denizens below. The top stack is 12, not 14, because it is 10 denizens plus 2 Visions; the aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ wording is explicitly identified as incorrect.
answers.evidence: Chronicle steps Vow an Oath and Citizenship state the choice and turnover; Rebuild world deck specifies ‘10 denizens + 2 random Visions = 12’ and calls the aid's ‘12 denizens + 2’ incorrect.
